Now that I have successfully read one image from each class, I can compare them to the test image.

*   **Test Image:** Green mango leaf with dark, somewhat circular necrotic lesions.
*   **Anthracnose (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg):** Shows a pale brown/yellowish leaf with some holes and damage. This doesn't match the distinct dark lesions of the test image.
*   **Die_Back (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg):** Shows a shriveled, dried, dark brown/black leaf. This is clearly different from the test image.
*   **Powdery_Mildew (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg):** Shows a leaf with white, powdery fungal growth. This is not what is seen in the test image.
*   **Sooty_Mould (Mango_Leaf_147.jpg):** Shows a leaf covered in a black, sooty, dusty-looking substance. This also doesn't match the distinct necrotic lesions of the test image.

My initial assessment was that the lesions are necrotic or discolored. None of the first reference images directly match the appearance of the test image, but Anthracnose often presents with dark spots. Let me view another reference image for Anthracnose and then explore the other classes more.

This second Anthracnose image is a strong match. I will still use my remaining budget to view more images, starting with other classes to confirm, then more Anthracnose if needed.

I have 3 views remaining. I have seen images from all four classes. The Anthracnose (Mango_Leaf_24.jpg) is the closest visual match. To further confirm, I will view the third Anthracnose image.

*   **Test Image:** Green mango leaf with dark, somewhat circular necrotic lesions.
*   **Anthracnose (Mango_Leaf_383.jpg):** This image also shows a green/yellowish mango leaf with distinct, dark brown to black, somewhat circular necrotic lesions. This also looks very similar to the test image.

Both `Mango_Leaf_24.jpg` and `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` from the Anthracnose class are very strong visual matches to the test image. The lesions on these reference images, particularly their color, shape, and distribution, closely resemble those in the test image. The other classes (Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, Sooty_Mould) consistently show different symptoms (shriveling, white powdery growth, or black sooty coating) that do not match the test image.

I have used 7 out of 8 reference image views. I need to use one more. I will view another Sooty Mould to be absolutely sure.
